Suppose that $r\in[1,2]$ and $0<\delta\le1/4$, and that $$u_r(x)\ge u_{r-\delta}(x),\qquad u_r(x)\ge u_{r+\delta}(x).$$ There is a probability density $k$ supported on $[r-\delta,r+\delta]$, bounded by $C/\delta$, such that $$K(y)=\int k(t)\mathbf1_{B(x,t)}(y)\,dt$$ satisfies $$\label{eq:local-zero-moment}
\int K(y)\overline{y-x}\,dh(y)=0.$$ Moreover, $0\le K\le1$, $\mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(K)\le C/\delta$, $K=1$ on $B(x,r-\delta)$, and $K=0$ outside $B(x,r+\delta)$. The density may be chosen measurably in $(x,r)$.

Let $U,V$ be finite nonnegative measures, of masses $P,N$. There are nonnegative submeasures $\mu_+\le U$, $\mu_-\le V$, both of mass $d=\min(P,N)$, such that $$U-V=\rho+\mu_+-\mu_-,\qquad
 \rho(\mathbb R^2)=P-N,\qquad |\rho|(\mathbb R^2)=|P-N|.$$ The residual $\rho$ has constant sign. If $U,V$ are absolutely continuous and supported in a common closed set, so are all the constructed measures.

There is an absolute constant $C$ such that $$\sum_{k=1}^m\sum_{q\in V_k}a_q E_k(q)\le C V.
 \label{eq:neighbor-budget}$$
Set $c_*=(\tau/10)^2$. Suppose $q\in V_k$, $E_k(q)\le c_*$, and $|x-q|_{\infty}\le50r_k$. Then $(q,n_k)$ is good with $\mathbb P_x$-probability one.

For every real $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ and every $m\ge1$, the quantities constructed above satisfy $$\sum_{l=1}^m\sum_{q\in V_l}a_q
 \left[
   \sup_{x\in D(q)}\bigl(R_l(x)+R_{l+1}(x)\bigr)
   +\sum_{k=1}^l2^{k-l}
       \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\in D(q)}T_k(x)
 \right]
 \le C V.
 \label{eq:label-packing}$$ The constant is absolute and independent of $m$.

There is a finite positive measure $\mu$ on pairs consisting of a terminal path $(q_1,\ldots,q_m)$ and a birth level $B\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ such that, for every node $\xi$ at level $k$, $$\mu\{B\le k,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_k)=\xi\}=M_\xi.
 \label{eq:labels-node-occupancy}$$ In particular, $$\mu\{B\le k,\ q_k=q\}=a_q,
 \qquad \mu(\text{all particles})=A_m\le V.
 \label{eq:labels-vertex-occupancy}$$ Writing $y=q_m$ for the terminal position of a particle, its complete path obeys $$|y-q_s|_{\infty}<r_s\qquad(1\le s\le m).
 \label{eq:labels-path-locality}$$ The path is defined also at levels preceding its birth.

The particle measure satisfies $$\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\xi\text{ intrinsically marked}}M_\xi&\le C V,
 \label{eq:labels-mark-budget}\\
 \int\sum_{s=B}^m E_s(q_s)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu&\le C V,
 \label{eq:labels-particle-energy}\\
 \int\sum_{s=B}^m R_s(y)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\mu&\le C V.
 \label{eq:labels-particle-switches}
\end{aligned}$$

Fix a particle, a level $1\le l\le m$, and $x\in D(q_l)$. Set $$c_s=R_s(y)+E_s(q_s),\qquad 1\le s\le m.$$ For $1\le k\le\min(l+1,m)$, $$R_k(x)+T_k(x)
 \le C\sum_{s=1}^k2^{s-k}c_s.
 \label{eq:labels-spatial-comparison}$$ The assertion for $R_k$ holds at every $x$ in the specified set, and the assertion for $T_k$ holds almost everywhere there. The constant is uniform over particles, $l$, and $x$.

Let $BV(\mathbb R^2)$ denote the globally integrable functions whose distributional derivatives have finite total variation. For every real $f\in BV(\mathbb R^2)$, $$Mf\in L^2(\mathbb R^2)\cap BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2), \qquad |D(Mf)|(\mathbb R^2)\le C|Df|(\mathbb R^2),$$ with the constant from Theorem 1. Writing $P(F)=|D\mathbf 1_F|(\mathbb R^2)$ for perimeter, every measurable set $E$ with $|E|<\infty$ and $P(E)<\infty$ satisfies $$\int_0^1 P(\{M\mathbf 1_E>t\})\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}t\le CP(E).$$ These superlevel sets have finite measure for every $t>0$ and finite perimeter for almost every $t>0$.

For real $u\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$ there are real $u_j\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ converging to $u$ in $W^{1,1}$, and $$\label{eq:appendix-translation}
 \|u(\cdot+z)-u\|_1\le |z|\,\|
abla u\|_1
 \qquad(z\in\mathbb R^2).$$ Moreover $|u|\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$ with $|
abla|u||\le|
abla u|$ almost everywhere. If $\chi$ is smooth and compactly supported, then $\chi u\in W^{1,1}$ and $
abla(\chi u)=\chi
abla u+u
abla\chi$. For locally Lipschitz real functions $v,w$, their maximum is locally Lipschitz and satisfies, almost everywhere, $$\label{eq:appendix-maximum}
 
abla\max(v,w)=
  egin{cases}
  
abla v,&v>w,\
  
abla w,&w>v,\

abla w,&v=w.
 \end{cases}$$ Products of locally Lipschitz functions satisfy the weak product rule. Their weak derivatives agree almost everywhere with their classical derivatives.

For every real $u\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$, $$\|u\|_2^2\le\|\partial_1u\|_1\|\partial_2u\|_1,
 \qquad\text{in particular }\|u\|_2\le\|\nabla u\|_1.$$

For a square $Q$ of side length $t>0$ and $u\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$, write $u_Q=|Q|^{-1}\int_Qu$. Then $$\label{eq:appendix-poincare}
 \int_Q|u-u_Q|\le Ct\int_Q|
abla u|.$$ For every grid square $Q$ of side $t$, there is a smooth cutoff $\chi_Q$ equal to one on the closed concentric dilation $3Q$, supported in the interior of $5Q$, with $0\le\chi_Q\le1$ and $|
abla\chi_Q|\le C/t$. With $c_Q=u_{5Q}$, it satisfies $$\label{eq:appendix-localization}
 \|
abla[\chi_Q(u-c_Q)]\|_1
       \le C\int_{5Q}|
abla u|.$$ Every disk of radius at most $t$ centered in $Q$ lies in $3Q$. The dilations $5Q$ of grid squares have bounded overlap. If the squares under consideration meet $O\subset\{x:\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(x,K)<t\}$, all their dilations $5Q$ lie in $\{x:\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(x,K)<6t\}$. Constants are independent of $Q,t,u,O,K$.

Suppose $u_j\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2)$ converge locally in $L^1$ to $u$, and $\sup_j\int_{\mathbb R^2}|\nabla u_j|\le M<\infty$. Then the distributional gradient of $u$ is a finite vector Radon measure $H$, with $$\label{eq:appendix-local-lsc}
 |H|(\mathbb R^2)\le M,\qquad
 |H|(O)=\mathcal V(u;O)
       \le\liminf_j\int_O|\nabla u_j|
 \quad\text{for every open }O.$$ If $|H|(K)=0$ for every compact Lebesgue-null set $K$, then $H=G\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}x$ for some $G\in L^1(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R^2)$ and $\|G\|_1=|H|(\mathbb R^2)$. In that case $u\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, with weak gradient $G$.
